name: SCARR, Paul Martin

headline.note: The Parliamentary Handbook supplies a detailed private legal and PanAust chronology, and employer records corroborate the executive role. PanAust changed from an ASX-listed private enterprise to control by a Chinese provincial state-owned company on 20 July 2015. Published sources do not establish hours, leave or exact boundaries for most roles, so senior titles and Scarr's aggregate statement of 25 private-sector years are not converted into full-time headline totals.

career_spells.role: Bachelor of Laws (Honours) and Bachelor of Commerce student
career_spells.evidence_note: Official and party biographies identify both University of Queensland degrees; the LNP biography says he graduated in 1991. Commencement dates are not published.
The Parliamentary Handbook gives Allens articled-clerk service from 1992 to 1993; Scarr's first speech corroborates joining Allens after graduation.
career_spells.counting_note: Year-only dates, hours, leave and exact appointment boundaries are not published.

career_spells.evidence_note: The Parliamentary Handbook gives Brisbane solicitor and senior-associate service from 1994 to 1999 and admission in Queensland in 1994. PanAust's annual report and Scarr's first speech corroborate prior Allens private practice.
career_spells.counting_note: The employer and years are supported, but full-time status, hours, leave and exact boundaries are not.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography gives 1999-2001 and admission in Papua New Guinea in 1999. Scarr's first speech says he lived and worked in PNG between 1999 and 2001; PanAust's report corroborates PNG admission and Allens practice.
career_spells.counting_note: Hours, leave and exact transfer and return dates are not published.

career_spells.evidence_note: The Parliamentary Handbook gives Brisbane senior-associate service from 2002 to 2005; PanAust's annual report corroborates earlier Allens private practice.
career_spells.counting_note: The unexplained 2001-2002 transition, exact dates, hours and leave remain unresolved.

career_spells.employer: Mallesons Stephen Jaques, now King & Wood Mallesons, Brisbane
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography lists King & Wood Mallesons from 2005 to 2007; the contemporary PanAust report uses the firm's then-name Mallesons Stephen Jaques. The LNP biography corroborates work at both major law firms.
career_spells.counting_note: Exact appointment/cessation, hours and leave are not published.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography gives both roles from 2007, with company-secretary service ending in 2015. PanAust's 2014 annual report gives an exact company-secretary appointment of 23 February 2007 and describes responsibility for legal, governance and secretarial functions. The company remained ASX listed until June 2015 and became wholly owned by Guangdong Rising on 20 July 2015.
career_spells.counting_note: The private-enterprise period is bounded by the control change, but the general-counsel start day, company-secretary cessation, hours and leave are unresolved.

career_spells.employer: PanAust Limited, controlled by Guangdong Rising Assets Management
career_spells.evidence_note: PanAust's official history says it became wholly owned on 20 July 2015 by Guangdong Rising H.K., a subsidiary of a Chinese provincial state-owned company. Employer reports list Scarr as general counsel at 1 January 2017 and 1 January 2019, with a successor listed by April 2019. The Parliamentary Handbook gives the endpoint only as 2019; Scarr describes 12 years in the role before Parliament.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control after 20 July 2015 is established, but the exact 2019 cessation, hours and leave are not.

career_spells.role: Director of subsidiaries and related companies in multiple countries
career_spells.evidence_note: The LNP biography says Scarr served as a director of companies in Laos, Thailand, Myanmar, Singapore, Chile, PNG and Australia while at PanAust. Entity-specific appointment dates, remuneration and workload are not supplied, and corporate control changed in 2015.
career_spells.counting_note: Subsidiary governance is excluded and must not be double-counted with executive employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary records show election to the Senate commencing 1 July 2019.

research_notes: Obtain exact commencement, cessation, hours and leave for each Allens and Mallesons/KWM role, including the 2001-2002 interval and internal transfers.
Confirm the exact general-counsel appointment date and company-secretary cessation date at PanAust; 23 February 2007 is documented only for company secretary.
Resolve Scarr's exact general-counsel cessation between 1 January and April 2019, along with hours, leave and campaign arrangements.
Confirm every PanAust group directorship, appointment/cessation, remuneration and whether it was inherent in executive employment.

Do not count the party biography's aggregate '25 years in the private sector' as documented full-time years; it spans PanAust's 2015 transition to foreign state ownership and supplies no hours or leave.
